source.title: L0 is not a neutral hyperparameter

record.tranche_reason: Tests a related feature-mixing mechanism in toy sparse autoencoders, using synthetic correlated features rather than measuring polysemantic neurons in a trained model.
record.gate_note: The reported results measure whether SAE latents recover or mix known toy-model features as SAE L0 changes. They do not measure neuron polysemanticity in vision or language models. Results cited from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: The study trains sparse autoencoders on a synthetic toy dataset and asks how SAE L0 affects whether SAE latents recover known features. The units studied are SAE dictionary latents, not neurons of a vision or language model, and the network under study has no neurons. SAE latents mixing correlated features is a related but different construct. The study relies on the superposition/SAE framework as a tool and reports its own method's behaviour, including a multi-L0 loss. Its results are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: SAE L0 is not neutral. Too-low L0 causes feature hedging, which gives better MSE than the correct features. Too-high L0 causes degenerate latents. Mixing a low-L0 and a high-L0 loss can recover the true features.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a synthetic correlated-feature dataset and Global BatchTopK SAEs to study latent recovery as L0 varies; it does not use the original neuron-visualization or neuron-testing methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Latent recovery varies with SAE L0 relative to the toy model's true L0. In the combined-loss experiment, the result differs between lambda 1 and lambda 20.

fits_no_version.finding: In a 20-feature correlated toy dataset, a 20-latent BatchTopK SAE recovers the true features at L0=5. Below the true L0, latents mix f0 into the others, and this is worse at L0 3 and for high-frequency latents. Above the true L0, latents degenerate without hedging. A combined L0 4/8 loss at lambda 20 recovers the true features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE latents become mixtures of correlated features when the SAE's L0 budget is below the data's true L0, even when SAE width equals the feature count.

record.problems: The evidence is from a single synthetic toy setup with correlated features and 20 latents, not trained language or vision model neurons. Most latent-recovery outcomes are qualitative; no uncertainty estimates are reported.

untested.parts: No network whose neurons are fewer than its features is examined. The SAE has as many latents as features.
No network neurons are studied. Initialization, regularization and noise are not varied.
No activation functions or architectures are compared, and no task performance is measured.
Activation ranges and explanation scoring are not varied.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V3 'tests' link conflates SAE latent mixing with network neuron polysemanticity. No row measures neurons of a trained model, so no verdicts are given. One loose analogy is with V4 (mixing without width pressure), but it concerns the SAE tool, not model neurons.

versions.untested_parts: No image classifier neurons or image inputs are studied.
No transformer language models or token/context responses are studied.
The study tests feature mixing in toy SAEs when the L0 activity budget is mismatched, not whether real networks represent more features than neurons or how common polysemantic neurons are.
Initialization, regularization, and training noise as causes of polysemantic neurons with sufficient neurons are not tested.
The study varies SAE L0 and combines L0 losses, but does not compare activation functions, architectures, or regularization methods, nor measure model performance on a task.
No real neuron is reinterpreted as detecting a shared feature such as pose.
The study does not vary activation ranges or explanation-scoring methods.

rows.subject: Global BatchTopK SAE
rows.stage_stated: trained on samples from the toy model
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SAE L0 set to 5, matching the toy model's approximate true L0.
rows.measure: Recovery of the toy model's underlying features
rows.value: The SAE perfectly learns the true features.
rows.locator: Case 1: SAE L0 = Toy Model L0
rows.note: A matched-L0 comparison condition; the report says the latent features are recovered without the described mixing.
rows.check: Measures SAE latent recovery at matched L0, not network neurons; bears on no version.

rows.subject: Global BatchTopK SAE
rows.stage_stated: trained on samples from the toy model
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SAE L0 below the toy model's true L0.
rows.measure: Mixing of underlying features in SAE latents
rows.baseline: Matched-L0 SAE at L0 5 recovers the true features.
rows.value: The SAE merges f0 into all other latents and no longer represents f0 in its own latent; higher-frequency latents appear more broken.
rows.locator: Case 2: SAE L0 < Toy Model L0
rows.note: The authors describe this as feature hedging.
rows.check: SAE latents mix f0 into other latents at L0 4. This is SAE feature hedging, not neuron polysemanticity. SAE width equals the feature count, so it is not a superposition test of V3.

rows.subject: Global BatchTopK SAE
rows.stage_stated: trained on samples from the toy model
rows.operation_detail: Compared MSE using a matched-L0 SAE cut to four active features with MSE using an SAE trained at L0 4.

conditions.value: matched-L0 SAE cut to k=4 versus SAE trained with k=4

rows.baseline: 0.53 (correct SAE trained with k=5 and cut to k=4)
rows.note: The lower MSE is reported for the SAE with broken/mixed latents.
rows.check: MSE comparison between two SAEs (0.53 vs 0.42). This is a mechanism check for the SAE objective, not a rate of polysemantic neurons.

rows.subject: Global BatchTopK SAE
rows.stage_stated: trained on samples from the toy model
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SAE L0 further below the toy model's true L0.
rows.measure: Mixing and breakage of underlying features in SAE latents
rows.baseline: SAE L0 4: f0 is mixed into other latents, with high-frequency latents more broken.
rows.value: Feature mixing is greater than at L0 4; latents for features 1-10 are described as completely broken.
rows.note: The post says the magnitude of mixing is higher than at L0 4.
rows.check: SAE latent mixing at L0 3; same construct issue as r2.

rows.subject: Global BatchTopK SAE
rows.stage_stated: trained on samples from the toy model
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SAE L0 above the toy model's true L0.
rows.measure: Incorrect or mixed features in SAE latents
rows.baseline: SAE L0 5: true features are recovered.
rows.value: Some slightly broken latents; no sign of systematic hedging.
rows.locator: Case 3: SAE L0 > Toy Model L0
rows.note: The authors attribute the imperfect result to multiple ways of achieving perfect reconstruction loss.
rows.check: SAE latent degeneracy at L0 6; not neurons.

rows.subject: Global BatchTopK SAE
rows.stage_stated: trained on samples from the toy model
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SAE L0 further above the toy model's true L0.
rows.measure: Incorrect or mixed features in SAE latents
rows.baseline: SAE L0 6: some slightly broken latents, with no systematic hedging.
rows.value: Latents are described as much more broken, with most completely broken; no sign of systematic hedging.

rows.subject: Global BatchTopK SAE
rows.stage_stated: trained with combined low- and high-L0 losses
rows.operation_detail: Trained using a sum of losses at two L0 values.
rows.measure: Recovery of underlying features and feature mixing
rows.baseline: Single-L0 cases: L0 4 causes hedging; L0 8 causes extensive latent breakage.
rows.value: A dedicated latent for f0 is retained, but clear hedging remains.
rows.locator: Mixing high and low L0 penalties together
rows.check: Performance of the authors' own multi-L0 SAE method; not a measure of polysemantic neurons.

rows.subject: Global BatchTopK SAE
rows.stage_stated: trained with combined low- and high-L0 losses
rows.operation_detail: Trained using a sum of losses at two L0 values.
rows.measure: Recovery of underlying features and feature mixing
rows.baseline: At lambda 1, a dedicated f0 latent remains but clear hedging persists.
rows.value: The true features are described as perfectly recovered.
rows.locator: Mixing high and low L0 penalties together
rows.note: The post says the combined losses address both high-L0 degeneracy and low-L0 hedging.
rows.check: The authors' own multi-L0 method recovers the true features at lambda 20; this is method performance, not neurons.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: SAE L0 below the toy model's true L0
reader_labels.reason: Under an insufficient L0 activity budget, the SAE mixes correlated underlying features; the effect worsens at L0 3 and is also described in the below-5 training run (r2, r4, r9).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: L0 matched to or above the toy model's true L0, and combined-L0 training
reader_labels.reason: Feature recovery is perfect at matched L0, while excess L0 produces different latent degeneracies without systematic hedging; a combined-L0 loss also recovers the true features at lambda 20. These results suggest feature mixing depends on the activity budget and training objective, not only on feature count exceeding latent count (r1, r5, r6, r8, r11).
